item.title: What ‘Hyperpolitics’ Explains About This Era
item.description:
Behind the intense political movements of the last decade, from Trumpism to wokeness and back again, there’s a strange and erratic rhythm. Movements saturate the culture seemingly overnight, only to evaporate or spark backlash just as rapidly. We’re extremely politically engaged, yet we’ve rarely felt so powerless to create lasting policy change. I haven’t seen many very successful attempts to explain what is driving this volatility. But one concept that has taken off recently, and captures what so many of us are feeling, is “hyperpolitics.” The idea comes from Anton Jäger, a historian and contributing writer to New York Times Opinion. In his book “Hyperpolitics: Extreme Politicization Without Political Consequences,” Jäger theorizes what it means to live in a moment marked by hyper-engage
Hyperpolitics names the rhythm: cultural saturation overnight, durable policy leverage almost never. Rhetoric craft for diagnosing why we're maximally engaged and still feel powerless — better than another doom clip.

item.title: We Can't Lose Control of A.I.
item.description:
Fears of out-of-control A.I. have reached a boil over the last few weeks, and several industry executives have called for a coordinated slowdown of A.I. development. But if our goal is to control A.I. — and that should be our goal — slowing down isn’t enough. We need to stop the labs from doing something they’re already on the cusp of doing: recursive self-improvement, or handing over the training of A.I. models to A.I. Mentioned: “ We’re Not Losing Control of A.I. We’re Giving It Away. ” by Ezra Klein You can find the transcript and more episodes of “The Ezra Klein Show” at nytimes.com/ezra-klein-podcast. Book recommendations from all our guests are listed at https://www.nytimes.com/article/ezra-klein-show-book-recs.html This episode of “The Ezra Klein Show” was produced by Marie Cascione, Emma Kehlbeck, Rollin Hu and Claire Gordon. Fact-checking by Marie Cascione, Isaac Scher and Julie
Why this sharpens your taste: Ezra Klein’s “We Can’t Lose Control of A.I.” is an actual argument about coordination and control — not a headlines dump. Craft move: treat the slowdown call as a governance design problem; track the claim structure, skip the doomscroll.
